newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's anti-inflation plan is realistic-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's anti-inflation plan is realistic-analyst.

text.p: The plan Hungary approved on Thursday to cut average inflation to 13 to 14 percent in 1998, is realistic, OTP Securities analyst Peter Bozso said.
"The 14 percent percent target is realistic," Bozso told Reuters, adding that this was a slight increase according to figures about which the Finance Ministry spoke earlier.

The ministry prepared two alternative anti-inflation programmes, with one of them aiming at a cut to slightly below 10 percent by December 1998 in year-on-year terms, while the other targeted levels of about 13 percent.

But only one proposal was submitted to the government, which forecasts 13 to 14 percent average CPI for 1998 -- down from an 18 percent target for this year -- and year-on-year inflation of 11 to 12 percent for December 1998, compared with a projection of 16 to 17 percent for December 1997.
The government said that a radical inflation cut could cool increasing economic growth.
He added that the one percentage point upward revision of the inflation forecast for 1998 to 14 percent was likely to make the government's inflation and economic growth forecasts more credible.
"Although the average inflation (in 1998) may be even higher than 14 percent due to the general elections," he said.
Hungary's inflation ran at 18.6 percent in April.
